exposure: Umbilical cord arterial pH and base excess values
Neonatal arterial pH and base excess values within 6 hours of life
Pathologic acidosis (pH ≤ 7.1) at birth or as a neonate
outcome: Direction and magnitude of change of pH and base excess between paired umbilical cord arterial and neonatal arterial blood samples
Composite outcome of death or cerebral palsy
cohort: The study included 102 intensive care unit neonates delivered between 2016-2020 at a single institution, who had paired umbilical cord arterial and neonatal arterial blood samples obtained within the first 6 hours of life.
finding: Changes in pH and base excess between delivery and the first newborn blood gas within 6 hours occurred over a wide range, with low birth weight, prematurity, or respiratory failure associated with less improvement, and neonatal acidosis (including that following normal birth values) significantly associated with increased morbidity and mortality.
